title: Winners a decade later
hook: Does an early small study settle what lottery wins do to satisfaction?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish the larger long-run lottery evidence from the blanket adaptation claim.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish the larger long-run lottery evidence from the blanket adaptation claim.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy satisfaction path starts one unit higher and retains 100% of that gain each year. What gain remains at year ten? Toy inputs A=[1, 1]; B=[1, 0.5].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[1, 1, 1], [1, 0.03125, 0.0009765625]]. Labels: Year 0 gain, Year 5 gain, Year 10 gain.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: An initial gain is compatible with either sustained or adapting paths, depending on the retention rule. The contrast makes the long-run assumption visible. A short follow-up alone cannot choose between these paths for real lottery winners.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Initial gain=1, Yearly retention=0.5. What is Year 10 gain? Answer: 0.001.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Initial gain=1, Yearly retention=0.5. What is Year 10 gain?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 0.001. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Large Swedish lottery winners reported higher life satisfaction for over a decade (Lindqvist, Östling & Cesarini, 2020).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish the larger long-run lottery evidence from the blanket adaptation claim.
